payload.recallText: I teach 3rd graders and it is the last unit of the year.  Prior to this I usually taught with the style of things being a little goofy and gamified.  Once my students got letters from a time machine.  Anyway, now I have to teach about the Oregon Trail.  This is more serious.  Still, I want to make it interesting and like a game.  For that I will combine the game you all know about called the Oregon Trail with D&D.  But even before that, I want to make this more realistic, so I take my kids out on a walk in downtown Manhatten.  It's hot.  It's a two mile walk.  Not super far, but maybe a stretch for some 9 year-olds.  Anyway, we start walking a pretend a little bit like we are on the Oregon trail.  The kids are getting thirsty and one spots a dirking fountain.  I want to make it realistic but there were no driking fountains on that trail.  But I also cannot let the kid not drink or I will be getting a call from a parent, so I say "Hey!  A stream!  Let's partake!"  Anyway, we finish the walk and get to the classroom bits.  I don't know if I can pull this off from a moral and historical standpoint, but I want them to feel it anyway, so I get serious and tell them there were real consequences, like dying.  At one point, a kid gets sick (in the game) and I roll and they are going to die, but another kid jumps in and says I am a doctor.  Years later I saw one of my students from the class named Karen.  She came up to me and you know what she reminisced about?  The Oregon Trail!
